answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 5 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the knoll hash is stored at intake, the thread graph groups the endorsements and the bridge audit shows the collapse. An operator copying one text across 115 aliases therefore pays for 115 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
